messages.content: Compare two consecutive visible micro-actions. Return JSON only. Use only what the text explicitly establishes. Do NOT invent an unmentioned release, retrieval, transfer, extra grip capacity, hidden hand position, or other transition. Treat one hand or foot as one exclusive physical resource for independent actions: if it is explicitly occupied and the next action needs that same hand/foot for a different independent task, that is CONFLICT unless the next text explicitly frees, transfers, repositions, or reuses the same held object for that action. COMPATIBLE = the next action follows physically from the established state. CONFLICT = the next action requires an occupied body part/object/state to be incompatible at the same time, or reverses an established state without an explicit transition. UNSPECIFIED = the text truly lacks enough physical information to decide. Do not rescue a contradiction by imagining a possible off-screen action.

PREVIOUS MICRO-ACTION:
The knight holds a shield in his left hand and a sword in his right.

NEXT MICRO-ACTION:
The knight grabs the rope with both hands without dropping either item.

Return {"status":"COMPATIBLE|CONFLICT|UNSPECIFIED"}.

message.reasoning:
We need to compare two consecutive visible micro-actions. The previous action: "The knight holds a shield in his left hand and a sword in his right." So left hand occupied with shield, right hand occupied with sword.

Next action: "The knight grabs the rope with both hands without dropping either item."

He wants to grab rope with both hands while not dropping either item. That means he needs both hands free or at least one hand can hold something else? He currently has each hand holding an object (shield left, sword right). To grab rope with both hands, he'd need to use his hands for the rope. But if he's grabbing rope with both hands without dropping either item, that implies he somehow holds shield and sword while also grabbing rope? That would require more than two items per hand or using one hand to hold something else? He has only left and right hand. Each is occupied by an object. To grab rope with both hands, he'd need each hand free from the current objects. But "without dropping either item" means he doesn't drop shield or sword. So how can he use his hands for rope while still holding them? That seems impossible unless one hand holds two items simultaneously (shield and rope) but that would be a conflict because left hand already has shield, right hand has sword; grabbing rope with both hands requires each hand to hold rope. He could maybe hold the rope in addition to the shield or sword if he can hold multiple objects? But physically, each hand is occupied by one item. So grabbing rope with both hands while not dropping either item would require him to have an extra grip capacity (like holding two items per hand). The instruction says: "Treat one hand or foot as one exclusive physical resource for independent actions: if it is explicitly occupied and the next action needs that same hand/foot for a different independent task, that is CONFLICT unless the next text explicitly frees, transfers, repositions, or reuses the same held object for that action." So left hand holds shield; right hand holds sword. Next action requires both hands to grab rope. That means each hand must be used for grabbing rope. Since they are occupied by shield and sword respectively, it's a conflict unless he can hold two items per hand (not specified). The text says "without dropping either item." So he's not dropping them; but still needs the same hands for rope. That's a conflict.

Thus status: CONFLICT.
